errors.text: The targeted property is misidentified: the hidden target seeks improved coercivity, specifically exceeding the roughly 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys, not cryogenic strength-ductility synergy or saturation magnetization.
The material is incorrectly reconstructed as a single-phase CrMnFeCoNi Cantor-type alloy rather than dual-phase FeCoNiTi containing fcc and C14 Laves phases.

The central orbital-moment challenge is misplaced onto Cr-induced moment cancellation. The target concerns understanding how the small fcc orbital moment contributes to coercivity through interaction with the C14 phase, spin canting, and domain-wall pinning.
The proposed composition tuning, cryogenic deformation, and SFE mechanism omit the decisive dual-phase microstructure and the compositionally matched C14-dominant control alloy.
The predicted outcome omits the key result of approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K and the distinct 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K magnetic transitions.
